messages.subject: information of regressions from ggplot?
parts:
Hello all,

If I am making a graph using ggplot, I can plot a trendline using geom_smooth()

For example:

df = data.frame(x=c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7), y= c(2,4,3,5,8,9,10))

p = ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm")



Is there a way of extracting the information on the linear model used to plot the line and standard errors? Coefficients and R2 and such? I can always just use the lm function, but it would seem to save a step if I could make ggplot report it for me.

--
Rosemary Hartman
roseh...@gmail.com
301-538-0136

parts:
Seems tricky. For one thing, `lm` itself isn't called till the plot is rendered which you can see from

debug(lm)
p = ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm") #nothing happens
p # dumps you into the debugger

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: information of regressions from ggplot?
parts:
An alternative strategy is to use the 'augment' method from package 'broom' to add columns to teh original data based on the lm fit. Then, you could run ggplot on that data and model fit data without geom_smooth.

But, if you'd rather try to get the model out of ggplot objects, the results from some poking around I just did may be helpful.

str(p$layers[[2]]$stat_params) # the 2 here will need to correspond with the geom_smooth layer...
List of 4
 $ na.rm  : logi FALSE
 $ method : chr "lm"
 $ formula:Class 'formula'  language y ~ x
  .. ..- attr(*, ".Environment")=<environment: 0x36e9110>
 $ se     : logi TRUE

You could maybe write a small function to run this fit on the data in the plot object. LIkely there's something in ggplot2 that would be useful for this, possibly the predictdf function: https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/blob/59c503b8e1cacf1f9264d1e233b7a305916905d6/R/stat-smooth-methods.r

Hope this helps,
